pr_title: Store the list of activated providers in the libctx
pr_body:
The provider config module was storing the list of activated providers
in a global variable. However, because different libctxs an each load
providers via config files we need to keep the list of activated providers
separate an in the libctx.

Partially fixes #15030

issue_context.title: OSSL_LIB_CTX_load_config() is not  thread safe
issue_context.body:
Some config modules seem to store information in global variables. However the config file may be loaded by multiple libctxs via the function `OSSL_LIB_CTX_load_config()`.

Notably, crypto/provider_conf.c stores the list of providers that it has activated in the global variable `activated_providers`. However, this can mean the list of activated providers can end up containing providers associated with different libctxs.

For example, if the default config file does not load any providers, but an application generated libctx uses a different config file and does load providers, then `activated_providers` will be populated with providers associated with application generated libctx. Subsequently the application will free the libctx, but `activated_providers` will still contain references to providers created under the application libctx. Finally, when the application exits, the auto-deinit code cleans up `activated_providers` and a use-after-free may occur.

It seems some other config modules  also use global variables so there may be issues there too although I haven't looked too closely. For example the SSL module has `ssl_names`, the engine module has `initialized_engines`.
comments: This is IMO fairly serious problem and should be resolved before beta1.
I have a fix for "provider_conf.c". I haven't analysed the other conf modules to see how big an issue these are.
